cards.headline: White 8 takes Black's stone at F18, so White's five stones are safe, and Black's ko retake threatens nothing. Black fails whatever the threats: S[DEAD], not S[KO+].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line, marked S[KO+]; the checker says DEAD. Black 7 takes the ko by capturing White 4 and puts White's five stones, White 2 among them, in atari at D19. But White 6 has left Black's stone at F18 one liberty, at F19. Black has nothing better at move 7: saving F18 at F19 loses the capturing race. White to play.

White 8 captures Black's stone at F18, so White's five stones gain a second liberty there; Black's D19 and F18 are both suicide. If Black 9 ataris White 8, White 10 connects to the outside wall. White can also take Black 9 at H19.
If Black 9 connects the ko at once, A16 and B16 make only one eye: White 10 plays inside, Black 11 takes it, and White 12 takes 14 stones.

diagrams.caption: After White 8 every Black move fails, Black 9 among them. White 10 takes Black's stone at E19, and White 12 retakes the ko for free, putting Black's group in atari at A16. Black 13 retakes after a ko threat elsewhere, but the capture threatens nothing, so White 14 plays elsewhere. Black 15 has no useful move: with B16 filled, connecting at A18 is self-atari. White 16 retakes for free. Each round costs Black a threat and White none; when Black runs out, White 18 takes 12 stones.

text: Black 7 threatens to take White's five stones at D19, but White 8 captures the stone at F18 first. That gives them a second liberty: Black's D19 and F18 are both suicide, and White answers an atari on White 8 by connecting (Diagram 2). Any other White move, except a retake at A18 after a threat, lets Black take the five stones and live. The tree's other S[KO+] leaf differs: there Black's own G18 at move 3 gives F18 two liberties, so the ko reads as real.

What remains is the ko at A18, and it cannot save Black. Black's retake threatens nothing: connecting at A18 fills Black's own eye, and A16 and B16 make only one eye (Diagram 3). So White waits a move and retakes without a threat, while White's capture always threatens to kill: Black pays a threat every round and White none (Diagram 4). The line ends with Black's ko capture, but Black fails whatever the threats: a clean failure, never KO+. No open question applies; the leaf-convention question is only about a clean success.

In the checker's narrow area Black fails even with eight threats more than White. Its wider area, which adds only points behind White's wall, leaves the leaf undecided, but after White 8 Black fails there with equal threats, which rules out KO+.

No move's grade changes: Black 3, at A19, is already wrong, since Black lives with A18 or F19 there in the tree; it will show DEAD instead of KO+. That DEAD is only the value of the tree's one line after Black 3: most alternatives to Black 5 stayed undecided, and a better one would be a missing branch.
